w: Family-run Sunnyvale institution open since 1979 and still the South Bay's benchmark for Persian charcoal kababs; order the kabab koobideh, succulent ground-lamb skewers over saffron chelo rice with grilled tomato. One of the most beloved Iranian tables in the Valley.
sources: https://www.yelp.com/biz/chelokababi-persian-cuisine-sunnyvale — 1,400+ reviews, updated Aug 2026, OPEN; est. 1979; address 1236 S Wolfe Rd

w: Upscale white-tablecloth Persian room on the Peninsula, chandeliers and Persian carpets, listed in the Michelin Guide; go for the crackly saffron tahdig ladled with gheimeh and the joojeh and koobideh kababs. Belmont day-trip worth the drive.
sources: Listed in the MICHELIN Guide — San Francisco Peninsula (guide update Oct 14 2025)
https://www.yelp.com/biz/shalizaar-belmont — updated Dec 2025, OPEN; 300 El Camino Real, Belmont

w: The famous Levantine anchor of Sunnyvale's Murphy Avenue restaurant row, always packed; the slow-braised lamb shank over rice, the muhammara and the hummus made it a South Bay date-night standard. Modern Middle Eastern done at a high level.
sources: https://www.yelp.com/biz/dishdash-sunnyvale — 4,800+ reviews, updated Aug 2026, OPEN; 190 S Murphy Ave

w: The University Avenue original of the beloved Israeli mini-chain, where silky made-daily hummus arrives warm topped with ful, mushrooms or lamb and mopped with fresh pita. A Palo Alto staple whose lines say it all.

address: 135 El Camino Real, San Carlos, CA 94070
w: Long-running Afghan favorite on the Peninsula (a Sunnyvale sibling too), where the kabuli palaw heaps raisins and carrots over lamb-scented rice and the steamed mantu dumplings come under garlic yogurt and meat sauce. Halal, generous, San Carlos day-trip.
sources: https://www.yelp.com/biz/kabul-afghan-cuisine-san-carlos — 1,890+ reviews, updated Jul 2026, OPEN; 135 El Camino Real, San Carlos

w: A tiny beloved Sunnyvale counter turning out crisp-shelled falafel and an overstuffed sabich (fried eggplant, egg, hummus, amba) in pillowy pita. Cult following, cash-quick, one of the Valley's best cheap Middle Eastern eats.
sources: https://www.yelp.com/biz/falafel-stop-sunnyvale — 3,100+ reviews, updated Jul 2026, OPEN; 1325 Sunnyvale Saratoga Rd

w: San Jose's best-known Ethiopian table, with a traditional mesob-seated room; scoop the spice-deep doro wat, kitfo and veggie combos with spongy injera. The South Bay's go-to for East African cooking.
sources: https://www.yelp.com/biz/zeni-ethiopian-restaurant-san-jose — 2,000+ reviews, updated Aug 2026, OPEN; 1320 Saratoga Ave

address: 801 W El Camino Real, Ste B, Mountain View, CA 94040
w: A 36-year-old Iranian grocery with a homey kabob counter in back — KQED called it a destination for Persian home cooking; get the charcoal koobideh plate with tahdig, then shop the shelves of Iranian pantry staples on the way out.
sources: https://www.kqed.org/arts/13965475/rose-market-iranian-persian-food-mountain-view — KQED feature: 'homey destination for Iranian food'
https://www.yelp.com/biz/rose-international-market-mountain-view-3 — updated Aug 2026, OPEN; 801 W El Camino Real, Ste B

address: 1910 W El Camino Real, Ste D, Mountain View, CA 94040
w: A Mountain View Persian mainstay locals rate for juicy joojeh (saffron chicken) kabob, koobideh and crispy tahdig paired with ghormeh or gheimeh stew. Halal, unfussy, consistently good.
sources: https://www.yelp.com/biz/caspian-restaurant-mountain-view-2 — 1,140+ reviews, updated Aug 2026, OPEN; 1910 W El Camino Real, Ste D

w: A cornerstone of Fremont's 'Little Kabul' since 1993, featured on Bizarre Foods and ABC7; the char-edged chapli kabob, kabuli palaw and crisp-fried bolani draw Afghan families from across the Bay. The definitive Little Kabul day-trip.
sources: https://www.yelp.com/biz/de-afghanan-kabob-house-fremont-3 — 650+ reviews, updated Aug 2026, OPEN; 37405 Fremont Blvd, Fremont; feat. Bizarre Foods America

dish: ca phe sua da (Vietnamese iced coffee)
w: A Milpitas Vietnamese coffee specialist beloved for its strong, sweet ca phe sua da and a viral banana latte, brewing from early morning to late night. The non-San-Jose spot for a proper Vietnamese caffeine hit.
sources: https://www.yelp.com/biz/da-vien-coffee-milpitas — 410+ reviews, updated Jul 2026, OPEN; 279 W Calaveras Blvd, Milpitas

address: 2047 El Camino Real, Santa Clara, CA 95050
w: The Santa Clara outpost of the Tay Ho name that made banh cuon its calling card — gossamer steamed rice sheets rolled around minced pork and wood-ear mushroom, made to order with cha lua and nuoc cham. A specialist worth crossing town for, outside the San Jose cluster.
sources: https://www.yelp.com/biz/banh-cuon-tay-ho-santa-clara — updated 2026, OPEN; 2047 El Camino Real, Santa Clara

w: A Milpitas neighborhood Vietnamese kitchen whose bun rieu — tomato-bright broth thick with crab-and-pork rieu, tofu and morning glory — is the reason regulars keep coming back, alongside solid pho. Non-San-Jose bun rieu depth.
sources: https://www.yelp.com/biz/pho-nguyen-milpitas — 610+ reviews, updated Aug 2026, OPEN; 275 W Calaveras Blvd, Milpitas

address: 89 S Park Victoria Dr, Milpitas, CA 95035
w: A Milpitas dessert-drink stop where the che is made fresh daily — pandan jelly, red tapioca, taro paste and fresh young-coconut water layered into che ba mau over crushed ice. The sweet, cooling end to a Vietnamese meal, north of San Jose.
sources: https://www.yelp.com/biz/bambu-dessert-and-drinks-milpitas-5 — updated Apr 2026, OPEN; 89 S Park Victoria Dr, Milpitas

dish: cha ca la vong (turmeric-dill grilled fish)
address: 3005 Silver Creek Rd, Ste 138, San Jose, CA 95121
w: A cash-only, family-run East San Jose favorite since 2006 and one of the Bay Area's rare cha ca la vong specialists — turmeric-marinated fish sizzled tableside over dill and scallion, plus hard-to-find banh bot chien trung. A specialty pick, not a wave-1 Little Saigon spot.
sources: https://www.yelp.com/biz/thien-long-san-jose — 1,430+ reviews, updated Aug 2026, OPEN; 3005 Silver Creek Rd, Ste 138; est. 2006

dish: banh mi thit and drip ca phe sua da
w: A long-loved Sunnyvale banh mi and coffee shop (listed by Visit Silicon Valley) with crackly-crust baguettes, house drip Vietnamese coffee and handmade desserts. The go-to Vietnamese sandwich-and-coffee stop on the west side, away from San Jose.
sources: https://www.yelp.com/biz/cam-hung-sunnyvale — 1,580+ reviews, updated Jun 2026, OPEN; 903 Reed Ave, Sunnyvale
